title: The water level cannot read your coverage map.

slides.headline: One farm. A lot to watch.
slides.body: A water reading from the far paddock can shape the next job of the day.

slides.headline: The tower is somewhere else.
slides.body: Design around the paddock, terrain and sky view where the sensor actually works.

slides.headline: This reading changes the day.
slides.body: Separate urgent thresholds from routine readings that can store, batch or retry.

slides.headline: Make the whole design work.
slides.body: Match message paths to power, antennas and the behaviour required when offline.

slides.headline: Start with your far paddock.
slides.body: Bring one site's conditions into a Hybrid IoT readiness conversation.

technicalNotes.headline: What must leave the field now?
technicalNotes.body: Separate urgent thresholds from routine telemetry that can wait, batch or retry.

technicalNotes.headline: Where does the device really operate?
technicalNotes.body: Use property conditions, terrain and movement—not the nearest town—as the design input.

technicalNotes.headline: What is the power budget?
technicalNotes.body: Reporting frequency and network behaviour must fit the device's energy model.

technicalNotes.headline: What happens offline?
technicalNotes.body: Define local control, storage, retry and operator visibility before choosing the communications path.

technicalNotes.headline: Map the field conditions
technicalNotes.body: Turn operating reality into a Hybrid IoT readiness brief.
